ing: peeled, or tayer; use russet potato if unavailable
st: Season the chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt, the lime juice and half of the garlic. Marinate for 30 minutes.
Peel the taro and grate it on the fine side of a box grater into a bowl. Wear gloves if your skin gets itchy.
Stir [[0.5 cup]] of the orange juice, [[0.5 tsp]] nutmeg, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper into the grated taro to make a thick, wet paste.

Melt [[3 tbsp]] butter in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion, remaining garlic and chili for 4 minutes, then add the tomatoes and cook 5 minutes more. Add the chicken and brown it lightly for 5 minutes.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Spread half the taro paste in a baking dish, add the chicken and sauce, then top with the remaining paste.
Pour the remaining [[0.5 cup]] orange juice around the edges, cover with foil and bake for 50 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake 20 more minutes until the top is golden and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C). Rest 10 minutes, then serve.

ing: or green beans, cut in pieces
st: Boil the split peas in water for 30 minutes until soft, then drain and mash them roughly. Set aside for the filling.
Mix [[3 cup]] flour, [[1 tsp]] baking powder and [[1 tsp]] salt. Add [[1 cup]] warm water and [[1 tbsp]] oil. Knead for 5 minutes, then rest the dough for 30 minutes.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and garlic for 3 minutes, then stir in [[2 tbsp]] curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and brown for 5 minutes. Add the potatoes, beans, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[2 cup]] water.
Cover and simmer for 30 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) and the potatoes are tender.
Divide the dough into 6 balls and roll each into a thin round. Brush with a little of the remaining oil.
Cook each round in a hot dry skillet for 1 minute per side, brushing with oil, until blistered. Clap the hot roti between your hands to loosen the layers.
Serve the roti with the chicken curry, potatoes, beans and the mashed split peas on the side.
Soak the black-eyed peas in water for 1 hour, then drain. Rinse the salted beef well and cut it into chunks.
Put the salted beef, chicken and peas in a pot with [[5 cup]] water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 30 minutes.
Remove the chicken and beef. Pull the chicken off the bone in chunks once cool enough, discarding skin and bones.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and garlic for 4 minutes.
Add the rice, [[1 tsp]] salt, [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and the whole chili. Stir for 1 minute, then pour in the cooking broth with the peas until it covers the rice by 1 inch.
Add the meats back in. Bring to a boil, cover and cook on low for 20 minutes until the rice is tender.
Rest, covered, for 10 minutes. Remove the chili, fluff with a fork, and check the chicken is at 165°F (74°C) before serving.
Boil the noodles in water for 4 minutes or as the package says. Drain, rinse under cold water and toss with a little oil so they do not stick.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat. Stir-fry the chicken for 5 minutes until cooked through to 165°F (74°C). Remove to a plate.
Add [[2 tbsp]] oil. Stir-fry the onion and garlic for 2 minutes.
Add the cabbage and cook for 3 minutes until slightly soft.
Add the noodles, [[3 tbsp]] soy sauce, [[0.5 tsp]] ginger, [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and [[1 tsp]] salt. Toss for 3 minutes.
Return the chicken and add the bean sprouts. Toss 1 more minute, taste and adjust the soy sauce, then serve hot.
Break up any clumps in the cold rice with your fingers so it fries evenly.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat. Scramble the eggs for 1 minute, then remove them to a plate.
Add [[2 tbsp]] oil. Stir-fry the onion, garlic and chili for 2 minutes.
Add the chicken and cook for 6 minutes, stirring, until no pink remains and it reaches 165°F (74°C).
Add the rice and press it into the pan. Stir-fry for 5 minutes until hot and starting to crisp in spots.
Pour in [[3 tbsp]] soy sauce, [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Toss well for 2 minutes.
Fold the scrambled eggs back in, taste, and serve hot, topped with a fried egg if you like.
Put the chicken, onion, garlic, ginger, lemongrass and [[8 cup]] water in a large pot. Bring to a boil and skim off any foam.
Add [[1 tsp]] turmeric, [[2 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper. Reduce to low and simmer for 40 minutes.
Meanwhile, boil the eggs in water for 10 minutes, then cool in cold water, peel and halve them.
Lift out the chicken. When cool enough, shred the meat. It should reach 165°F (74°C) in the thickest part before shredding.
Strain the broth, return it to the pot and add the potatoes. Simmer for 15 minutes until tender.
Divide the chicken, bean sprouts and eggs among bowls. Ladle the hot broth over the top.
Top with sliced scallions and serve with rice or noodles.
Rub [[0.75 cup]] cold butter into [[2 cup]] flour and [[0.5 tsp]] salt with your fingers until crumbly. Stir in [[5 tbsp]] ice water to form a dough.
Wrap the dough and chill for 30 minutes.
Melt [[3 tbsp]] butter in a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrots for 5 minutes.
Add the chicken, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and cook 5 minutes. Sprinkle in [[0.5 cup]] flour and stir for 1 minute.
Slowly stir in [[1.5 cup]] broth and [[0.5 cup]] milk. Simmer for 10 minutes until thick, then add [[1 cup]] peas. Cool the filling for 15 minutes.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Roll out two-thirds of the dough and fit it into a pie dish. Add the filling.
Cover with the remaining dough rolled out, pinch the edges, cut a few steam slits and brush with the beaten egg.
Bake for 35 minutes until golden and the filling is bubbling at 165°F (74°C). Rest 10 minutes before slicing.
Rinse [[1 cup]] urad dal and soak it in water for 4 hours, then drain well.
Grind the dal in a blender with a few spoonfuls of water to a thick, fluffy paste. Add water only as needed, up to [[0.5 cup]].
Stir in [[0.25 cup]] flour, the onion, garlic, chili, [[1 tsp]] cumin, [[0.5 tsp]] baking powder and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Beat the batter hard with a spoon for 2 minutes to add air. It should hold its shape when scooped.
Heat [[3 cup]] oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Drop heaping tablespoons of batter into the oil, 5 or 6 at a time. Fry for 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with chutney or hot pepper sauce.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and flour a loaf or round cake pan.
Cream [[1 cup]] butter with [[1 cup]] sugar for 4 minutes until pale and fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then add [[1 tsp]] vanilla.
Whisk [[2 cup]] flour, [[2 tsp]] baking powder, [[0.5 tsp]] nutmeg and [[0.25 tsp]] salt together in another bowl.
Fold the dry mix into the butter mixture in two parts, with [[0.25 cup]] milk, until just combined.
Fold in [[1 cup]] raisins and [[0.5 cup]] almonds. Pour into the pan.
Bake for 55 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool in the pan for 15 minutes, turn out and cool fully before slicing.
